label: Reset gate dips for a1/S1 and a1-leaning policy, growing late in episode
terms: (phase == D2) * choice * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * choice * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1) * ep_trial
explanation: Raw reset gate r43 sits near 1 (mean 0.989) and dips mostly late in the episode; timing alone gives R^2 0.53. Past timing, every effect gets bigger with ep_trial (scaling the terms by ep_trial lifted dev R^2 from 0.37 to 0.42; exp and quadratic scalings did worse). D2: lower after choosing a1 and after reaching S1, and lower still when the policy logit leans to a1 (choice). This graded model term is the biggest single addition (dev 0.42 -> 0.56). D1: lower after a previous trial of a1 -> rare S2, especially when rewarded; also mildly lower with an a1-leaning policy. GO: slightly lower after a previous a1. Value and the trial before added little. 7 terms: dev 0.581, test R^2 beyond timing 0.578, roughly at the all ceiling of 0.58. An observed-only version (no choice logit; action/state/previous-trial terms) reached dev 0.47. Not explained: occasional big D1 dips (about -0.12) after a rewarded S2 trial that came after a switch or a loss.

issues: The score itself reproduces: test R^2 beyond timing is 0.578, which matches the 'all' ceiling of 0.58. The problem is with the claims made about it.

The claim that 'exp or quadratic scalings did worse' is false on test. With the same 7 terms, ep_trial**2 scores 0.582 and np.exp(ep_trial/25) scores 0.608, against 0.578 for linear ep_trial. Only the hinge versions do worse (max(ep_trial-60,0) 0.500, max(ep_trial-70,0) 0.474). The late-episode growth is steeper than linear.

The label and explanation lean on the policy logit (the 'a1-leaning policy' term, 'the biggest single addition'). But an observed-only set does better than the logit version. Using the D2 this-trial choice x state table, the D2 previous-trial choice x state table, the D1 last_is a1 S2 r/u terms, GO prev_action==1 and a D2 a1-after-a1 term, all scaled by ep_trial, gives test 0.586. With exp(ep_trial/35) scaling the same set gives test 0.620 (dev 0.618), above the authors' 0.578 and above the 'all' ceiling. The logit seems to stand in for recent choice/state history, which the agent can observe at D2. The authors' observed-only comparison (dev 0.47; test 0.425 when re-scored) left out previous-trial terms at D2, so it understated what observed variables can do.
'Mildly lower with an a1-leaning policy at D1' is essentially empty. Its weight is -3e-6, and dropping the term only moves test from 0.578 to 0.576.

Systematic errors remain at D2, and they are by previous-trial pattern. With the authors' terms, D2 after a1 S2 r is under-predicted by +0.008, D2 after a2 S2 u by +0.005, and D2 after a1 S1 u is over-predicted by -0.006. The worst windows are all at trials 92-99, where D2 dips to about 0.84 against predictions of about 0.92-0.93. That fits linear ep_trial scaling being too flat at the end of the episode.
The D1 dips at trials 93-99 (about -0.12 to -0.15, e.g. 0.82 actual vs 0.94 predicted) stay unexplained. The authors do note this.
